newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels spent up to $300,000 on assault - paper.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels spent up to $300,000 on assault - paper.

text.p: Marxist guerrillas spent between $200,000 and $300,000 on their takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, the Peruvian daily La Republica said on Thursday.
The money was spent on training, arms purchases and a $5,000 payment to each of the rebels involved in the Dec. 17 operation, the newspaper said, quoting local anti-terrorist police.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) got the money "through drug trafficking and for freeing kidnapped businessmen, both in the country (Peru) and in Bolivia," it added.
The assault was planned six months ahead of time from the rebels' Amazon jungle base, La Republica said.
About 20 heavily armed guerrillas were still holding 104 hostages at the residence on Thursday.
